perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective, here is what he knows:

- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual at work, and remembered her as usually vibrant.
- He asked if she was okay, and she said it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff.” She did not give details.
- He offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk, and she thanked him sincerely.
- During a lunch break, he overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He brought up financial planning and offered to discuss budgeting tips. Patricia said she had been feeling overwhelmed with her bills and would take him up on the offer soon.
- Afterward, he worried he might have overstepped, so he clarified that he only wanted to help, not pry. Patricia assured him she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful for his support.
- He told her he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend.
- Later, he checked in more casually. Patricia said everything was fine and she planned a quiet weekend at home; she didn’t share more about her personal situation.
- He continued to check in regularly at work. Patricia said she was busy but handling things, and that his support meant a lot to her.
- He has positioned himself as a supportive colleague and friend, offering help, listening, and respecting her boundaries.
